system.name: ACE (Adaptive Constrained Equivariance)
system.one_liner: Constrained optimisation that starts from a flexible non-equivariant model and gradually tightens it toward equivariance, following a homotopy from easy to hard problems.

content.variant_note: three training-stage snapshots of a network, its formula and a 3D loss landscape with trajectories, plus a homotopy sketch of three curves with gamma insets at the right
content.argues: Starting relaxed and tightening equivariance as γ decays lets training reach a better minimum than a strictly equivariant network trained from the same initialisation.
content.subject: Three training snapshots (network, formula, loss landscape with trajectories) and a homotopy sketch of three curves with γ insets.

lessons.what_to_learn: Redraw the same stack (network sketch, formula box, loss landscape) at a few training stages and let one term of the formula and the matching nodes fade, so the reader sees the relaxation being tightened; show a baseline trajectory in a second colour from the same start point.
lessons.suits: Optimisation, relaxation or curriculum-style methods whose point is how training moves through a loss landscape while a constraint or coefficient changes.

evidence: a relaxed, non-equivariant model that gradually becomes equivariant as the layer-wise coefficients γi decay.
The blue trajectory illustrates a strictly equivariant network feq trained from the same initialization.
the coefficient γ allows the training problem to transition between easier (non-equivariant) and harder (equivariant) problems, facilitating convergence.

summary: ACE (Adaptive Constrained Equivariance) trains a network that starts flexible and non-equivariant and is gradually constrained toward equivariance, following a homotopy from easy to hard problems. In the left half of Figure 1, three columns show the same network at three stages: a sketch whose yellow non-equivariant nodes fade, a formula box f(x) = f_eq(x) + γ_i f_neq(x) whose second term fades out, and a 3D loss landscape that gets rougher, where a red trajectory from a shared start point reaches a deep valley while a blue trajectory of a strictly equivariant network stays near the start; boxed waveforms show γ1 to γ3. The right half stacks three curve sketches with γ insets illustrating the transition between easy and hard problems.
summary_zh: ACE 先训练灵活的非等变网络，再随系数 γ 衰减逐步收紧到严格等变。图 1 左半三列分别画网络草图、公式（非等变项逐渐淡出）和越来越崎岖的损失地形，红轨迹抵达深谷，蓝轨迹（严格等变）停在起点附近；右半是三幅同伦曲线草图，配 γ 小框。
notes: model-anatomy is added as a minor third kind for the layer sketches. The two halves are counted as unlabelled panels because the caption names them Left and Right. How the dots, arrows and shaded span of the right-hand sketch map onto the easy and hard problems is read from the caption and the matching colours, not stated in the figure. That the blue trajectory is stuck near the start is read from the preview. The digest finds no placed bitmaps: surfaces and curves are vector shapes (thousands of mesh polygons) and formula text is outlined.
